_authority: How a free-form request picks a mode, and how RETROFIT is told apart from RESTYLE. SKILL.md points here; it must not restate the table in prose. The rules below are executable: retrofit/scripts/test_routing.py implements exactly this file and asserts the named cases.
_why: The pilot failure was not that Claude refused to upgrade a module. It was that the operator had to know the word 'retrofit' and which skills to route to. A colleague in Cowork types 'Redesign Module 1 using the NOVIKONTAS Course Factory' and that has to be enough - no skill names, no validator names, no folder architecture, no git.

modes.plan: an accredited programme exists, the modules do not. Design the delivery from scratch.
modes.retrofit: the course content exists as a built module. Keep the content; rebuild the delivery.
modes.restyle: the operator has named a NARROW cosmetic change and nothing else. Do that and stop.
modes.ship: a built course goes onto the two terminals.
modes.audit: check an existing course against the programme and the terminals; change nothing.

retrofit_triggers._match: Any ONE of these intents, in any language, about material that already exists. The phrases are examples, not a whitelist - match the intent.

examples: apply Course Factory to this module

intents.intent: make it like the reference product
examples: make my existing module like GAS BASIC
make it look like GAS BASIC
redesign this module using Course Factory
make this module much more visual and interactive
I already have the content, make it better

retrofit_triggers.requires: existing built material to work on - a module.html, a deck, a course folder. Without it this is a `plan` request about content that does not exist yet.

restyle_triggers._match: RESTYLE needs BOTH a narrow cosmetic target AND a scope limiter. Either one alone is not enough: 'change the colours and make it like GAS BASIC' is a retrofit; 'only change the colours' is a restyle.
restyle_triggers.behaviour: Do exactly the named change. Do not migrate the shell, do not re-compose screens, do not add visuals. Say in one line what a full retrofit would additionally do, and stop. The operator asked for a restyle; giving them a retrofit is not generosity, it is ignoring them.

ambiguous._rule: Ask only when the request is genuinely ambiguous about SCOPE, never about the A/B/C level - that is this skill's job to decide.
examples: make it better (no target named, no material identified)
fix the module (fix what - a defect, or the delivery?)
ambiguous.ask: one batched question naming the two readings, then proceed

language_lock._law: COURSE_LANGUAGE is mandatory in plan and retrofit alike. Course-facing output stays in it unless translation is explicitly requested.
detect_from: the existing course-facing files - module.html lang attribute, screen titles, task text
language_lock.values: a language name or a combination: English, Latvian, Norwegian, English+Latvian
language_lock.the_case_this_exists_for: A Latvian operator asks, in Latvian, to redesign an English module. The chat report may be Latvian. Every slide, task, handout, assessment and instructor cue stays English. Translating a course because the request arrived in another language destroys an accredited artefact.
language_lock.drift_check: retrofit/scripts/check_language.py compares course-facing files against the declared COURSE_LANGUAGE and reports files whose script or common-word profile disagrees.

routing_targets._rule: course-factory orchestrates. It does not write screens, visuals or tasks itself, and the operator never names these.
routing_targets.trainee_task_screens: course-task-ux (only when the module has tasks)
